note: Rationing rules as data, not constants scattered through fetch code. The reserve in provider_quota.PROVIDER_SPECS is a floor -- it stops a provider hitting zero. This is the budget: it decides who may spend while budget still exists. cfbd burned its whole 1,000-call month by 2026-08-10 and went dark for three weeks with the reserve working exactly as designed, because nothing rationed the month.

tiers.1: A fixture inside its lock window. A pick is about to be frozen permanently and cannot be revised, so this is the one call whose data quality is irreversible.
tiers.2: A fixture kicking off today. Wrong or stale data here is published to users while it matters.
tiers.3: Standings, rankings, tables. Visible, but a few hours stale changes nothing a reader would notice.
tiers.4: Leaders, talent, season backfill, advanced metrics. Slow-moving; a day stale is indistinguishable from fresh.

enforce_note: Advisory until a full period of spend accounting exists. The allowances below are derived from a ceiling and a calendar, not from measured behaviour, so enforcing them today would ration real calls against a guess -- the same mistake as the fixed cache TTLs this replaces. While false, budget_decision() still computes and reports every refusal it would have made, so a month of hindsight is available before anything is actually declined. Set true once usage_report() shows where the budget really goes.

cfbd.note: Free tier verified at 1,000/month. NCAAF plays Saturdays, so an even daily split starves the day that matters; day_share lets a game day borrow against the quiet days around it.

cbbd.note: No verified ceiling is configured, so no daily allowance can be derived. Enforcement stays reserve-only until a real ceiling is read off a live response.

odds_api.note: Ceiling is derived live from remaining+used, so the stored value is a fallback for a cold ledger.
